#Aletheia #HumanRights 🌐

In reality, outlawing asexuality penalizes people for simply not marrying or reproducing, imposing 5-10 years in prison to enforce authoritarian control over private life.

Niger's ruling junta broadened anti-LGBTQIA+ laws under Articles 25 and 390, imposing severe prison sentences and £130k fines on asexual individuals alongside the broader queer community.

The Bright Side:
Exposing this unprecedented legal ban forces global civil rights monitors to recognize how forced natalism and authoritarian population control threaten universal personal freedom.
The Plane Error swaps WHAT (protecting families) with WHO (punishing non-conforming individuals). The junta uses moral pretexts to justify total state ownership over body and personal life choices.

Social Physics Analysis:
The junta runs a Smart Selfish Maneuver by inventing a crisis around non-participation to justify intrusive state surveillance. They project moral decay onto peaceful citizens to hoard totalitarian power.

The Trajectory: The Path of Destruction.
Mapping the gap between moral protection claims and totalitarian incarceration plots a trajectory straight into Greater Evil, destroying fundamental individual liberty.

The Unavoidable Truth: A state that criminalizes doing nothing exposes its goal of total bodily control.
The Unavoidable Lie: Mandating marriage and childbirth under penalty of prison protects family values.

Alethekanon:
When a state penalizes absence of action, it transitions from regulating conduct to claiming total ownership of the human mind and body. This is structural despotism.

Awwthekanon:
No human being should ever live in fear of imprisonment simply for existing as they are. Targeting peaceful, harmless lives under the guise of morality is a heartbreaking cruelty.

Brothekanon:
Imagine putting someone in prison for ten years just for wanting to be left alone and minding their own business. That is beyond unhinged.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
Why Niger explicitly criminalising asexuality is significant to everyone, regardless of identity

To understand Nigers asexuality criminalisation, we should see this law as part of a bigger – and growing – global trend among conservatives about 'traditional families'

Actual Article Body:
In June 2026, the nation of Niger became the first nation in the world to criminalise asexuality, as part of a wider crackdown on the LGBTQIA+ community. The country, currently run by a military junta, broadened its anti-LGBTQIA+ laws, increasing the criminalisation of LGBTQIA+ ‘practices’ to include anyone who ‘attempts to’ participate.

The ILGA database says the newly passed laws, Article 25 and 390, are already having life-threatening implications on LGBTQIA+ people in Niger.

Ace people in Niger, alongside people of all LGBTQIA+ identities, can now face 5-10 years in prison and fines worth up to £130K.

The change was significant as it makes Niger the first country to name the asexual community in its law books. However, it begs the question: how does one ban an asexual “practice”, other than to punish people who are not married and those who don’t have babies? To understand, we should see this law as part of a bigger – and growing – global trend among conservatives.

Niger’s crackdown on asexual “practices” is not isolated to the West African nation; it’s part of a greater trend of anti-LGBTQIA+ rhetoric, enforced monogamy and anti-abortion movements worldwide.

In 2026, Niger (alongside Burkina Faso and Mali) has strengthened diplomatic ties with Russia, while their military juntas are at war with insurgent groups. This move comes at a time when Russia instituted a ban on “propaganda” that promotes childfree lifestyles. But this rhetoric is not isolated to countries we tend to associate with deep-rooted conservative laws.

Meanwhile, conservatives in the U.S. have been shaming childfree women as “childless cat ladies”. This builds on previous campaigns from the religious right in America, which stated the Respect for Marriage Act would lead to asexual marriages, which they believed would lead to a marriage “inferno”. Groups like the Heritage Foundation equated asexual marriages to “selfishness”.

Zoom out a little, and it's easy to see the hypocrisy of conservative religious people demonising asexuality, considering how much abstinence was preached to me growing up in a conservatively religious home.

Asexuality stands in direct contrast to the religious right’s shaming of ‘childfree’ people, which also often ignores other routes to having children like adoption, and family models that show you can be asexual and a parent. Instead, the decreasing birth rate has been a talking point of right-wing politics for years.

And yet, conservatives do not care to address the many concerns related to raising a child – such as rising costs of childcare, affordable housing, and lack of reproductive justice. They only seem to care about making everyone become a parent.

This change in the law in Niger should be seen in the context of attacks on everyone’s freedom to be their true self and design their life however they wish, free of societal, religious, or political pressure.

If they attack and pressure those who feel little to no sexual attraction or interest in sex, that is a gateway to attacking anyone who does have sex in any way that’s not “approved” or “acceptable”.

When there is so much hate out there, it's easy to get swept up in the doom.

QueerAF doesn't do that. We sprinkle in the joy that is the lifeblood of why being LGBTQIA+ is so simply wonderful.

And in the newsletter where this was first published, there was actually a bunch of positive news to celebrate. It shows me that despite the headlines knocking us down, we're getting right back up again and using our anger to fuel our fight.

While the rest of the media cashes in on hate about us, we can focus on queer joy - because you drive us. The community. QueerAF readers - not advertisers.

Our members directly fund our content. When you sign up, you get to have your say on how your funds are used. On what content we should commission.

But we turn down advertising and sponsorships in this newsletter so we can focus on delivering on content for you, not just clicks. That's why we need you to sign up to become a QueerAF member.

You'll join hundreds of awesome queer as f**k members who ensure we can keep our unique approach to queer content happen. If you want to see the media cover more stories about the joy in our lives - please, consider a membership. We can't run our outlet without you.
